Is this a known issue?

$ cat lean-toolchain
leanprover/lean4:v4.30.0-rc1

$ lake exe cache get
Current branch: feature/simple-graph/edegree
Using cache (Azure) from origin: SnirBroshi/mathlib4
Attempting to download 76 file(s) from leanprover-community/mathlib4 cache
Downloaded: 0 file(s) [attempted 76/76 = 100%, 1 KB/s], Decompressed: 0
Decompressed 0 file(s)
Attempting to download 76 file(s) from SnirBroshi/mathlib4 cache
Downloaded: 0 file(s) [attempted 76/76 = 100%, 0 KB/s], Decompressed: 0
Warning: some files were not found in the cache.
This usually means that your local checkout of mathlib4 has diverged from upstream.

  * If you push your commits to a PR to the mathlib4 repository
    (use a draft PR if it is not ready for review),
    then CI will build the oleans and they will be available later.
  * If you have already opened a PR, this may mean
    the CI build has failed part-way through building.
Decompressed 0 file(s)
Already decompressed 8175 file(s)

$ xxd .lake/build/lib/lean/Mathlib/Tactic/TacticAnalysis/Declarations.olean | head -1
00000000: 6f6c 6561 6e02 0134 2e32 392e 3000 0000  olean..4.29.0...

$ grep -Fl 4.29.0 .lake/build/lib/lean/Mathlib/**.olean | wc -l
112

$ grep -Fl 4.30.0 .lake/build/lib/lean/Mathlib/**.olean | wc -l
7814

The PR is #33501 and the build is indeed failing, but why doesn't it download the oleans from master? Especially when this is a basic file unrelated to the PR.
I know I can rm -rf .lake, just reporting in case this is a bug. I'll do it soon unless you want me to debug anything further.

Oh forgot to mention -- this causes the following error when trying to build:

failed to read file '.lake/build/lib/lean/Mathlib/Tactic/TacticAnalysis/Declarations.olean', incompatible header

So it destroys the build, won't even let me rebuild without nuking .lake
@Snir Broshi, can you provide instructions for reproducing, if possible?

Kim Morrison said:

Snir Broshi, can you provide instructions for reproducing, if possible?

This reproduces the issue:

git clone git@github.com:SnirBroshi/mathlib4.git repro -b temp/olean-issue-4.30 --depth 1
cd ./repro/
lake exe cache get
echo hello > .lake/build/lib/lean/Mathlib/Tactic/TacticAnalysis/Declarations.olean
lake build

Now no amount of lake exe cache get or lake build will avoid the invalid header error.

Of course in reality I didn't manually modify the olean, but I'm not sure how to naturally cause lake exe cache get to skip downloading it in the first place, but it did happen naturally. I guess this has something to do with the .olean.* files near it.
@Mac Malone what do we need to do here? Is it just adding a suggestion to run lake clean on invalid header errors?
@Kim Morrison I believe lake exe cache get! may be the solution here? It sounds like lake exe cache get messed up and then didn't redownload because there was already a file in the build directory.

lake exe cache get! does work, but isn't it pretty similar to rm -rf .lake or lake clean + lake exe cache get? I'm trying to avoid redownloading everything, and only fixing the outdated oleans.

Can I check why it didn't redownload? e.g. is some .hash file lying to it? Surely the existence of the olean in the build directory is not the issue per se, since e.g. upgrading the toolchain or git pull usually make lake exe cache get fetch the olean anyways

btw lake build -H and lake -H exe cache get don't fix the issue, so hash files might not be the issue
@Snir Broshi Note that you can scope lake exe cache get! to a particular file, as in lake exe cache get! Mathlib.Tactic.TacticAnalysis.Declarations

The issue is with 112 files. I can solve it with grep -Fl 4.29.0 .lake/build/lib/lean/Mathlib/**.olean | xargs ... but I still think there's an improvement to be had here.
The cache tool somehow caused an state from which it cannot recover without some form of reset (e.g. rm -rf .lake or lake exe cache get!).
I believe there's a way for lake exe cache get to notice that some of the oleans are old, and update them, I just don't know enough about the system to point to the exact issue, but I'm hoping you can help.

I can take a closer look when I have a chance. In general we don't want to invest a lot on lake exe cache now as we plan to move to lake cache for mathlib soon, I hope you understand. But hopefully this is not too complicated.

@Snir Broshi It was not clear to me in your case whether the problem was simply the build directory or a corrupt cache itself. If the cache is fine, you can use lake exe cache unpack! to skip donwloading and just force an unpack. lake exe cache get (and lake exe cache unpack), by default, do not clobber files already in the build directory.

Marcelo Lynch said:

In general we don't want to invest a lot on lake exe cache now as we plan to move to lake cache for mathlib soon

Oh I thought any improvements here will be upstreamed to the new cache tool, will they not? Or are you saying that the new tool already solves this issue?
lake exe cache and lake cache internally work very differently. Changes to one are not readily portable to the other.
The new tool should solve this issue as it uses Lake's own traces to validate aritfacts instead of lake exe cache's custom tracing mechanism.

Oh that's great! In that case I agree that fixing lake exe cache is not worth it, I reported this issue because I thought it would help others in the future, sorry for the noise and thanks!
btw unpack! does fix it, so the issue is that it thinks the existing olean is fine and doesn't replace it

This may be a different issue, but I pushed a commit to #37812 that only changes test files and this seems to have caused some Mathlib.Init oleans not to be downloaded anymore: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/actions/runs/24172001102/job/70545399848?pr=37812#step:18:27
